descriptionChirho: The abstract quality of being set apart, sacred, or consecrated to God; the divine attribute of holiness itself, often in construct chains like 'spirit of holiness' or as a predicate ('is holy'); Arabic quds and Swahili utakatifu (u-class abstract) confirm the abstract sense.

A sacred location set apart for worship, especially the tabernacle sanctuary or temple inner chamber (the Holy Place); Arabic cognate maqdis and Swahili pa-takatifu (locative class) confirm the spatial sense.
God's holiness or a person's holiness expressed with a pronominal suffix (his/my/your/our holiness), referring to the divine or human quality of consecrated apartness as a possessed attribute.

A concrete item that has been consecrated or set apart as sacred, including individual offerings, dedicated objects, and firstfruits; Arabic muqaddas and Swahili ki-takatifu (thing class) confirm the object sense.

Multiple consecrated items, sacred contributions, or dedicated offerings viewed collectively; the Arabic plural aqdas and Swahili vi-takatifu (plural thing class) mark this as the concrete plural of sacred objects.

The superlative construct chain qodesh qodashim (holy of holies), designating either the innermost sanctuary or items of the highest degree of consecration; identified by construct-chain grammar (N-msc + N-mp) and glosses like 'most holy' or 'holiest of'.
